match.reason: None of the bank points teaches natural selection itself: the closest, on genetic diversity, is about why variation matters and is broader than the new point, while the others cover gene flow, drift, allele frequency or diversity loss.

draft.title: Natural selection
card: Individuals in a population differ in their traits. Many of these differences are inherited, because they come from different alleles.
Some traits suit the environment better than others. Individuals with these traits are more likely to survive and reproduce.
They pass their alleles to more offspring than other individuals do. Over generations, those alleles become more common in the population.
Selection acts on traits that already exist. It does not make new alleles, and an individual does not change its alleles to suit the environment.
draft.remember: Suited individuals leave more offspring, so their alleles become more common.

a.q: Which statement best describes natural selection in a population?
opts: Individuals with suited traits leave more offspring
Individuals gain alleles that they need to survive
Individuals with suited traits live longer lives only
Individuals pass on traits gained during their lifetime
a.why: Natural selection works because suited individuals reproduce more, so their alleles spread. Gaining alleles on demand is wrong, because selection acts on variation that already exists. Living longer alone does not change allele frequencies unless it leads to more offspring.
a.clue: What do suited individuals pass on, and how much?

b.q: Some beetles on a Victorian farm have an allele for dark green bodies. Birds find them harder to see on the dark leaves. Over many generations, what is most likely to happen?
opts: The dark green allele becomes more common
Each beetle changes colour to match the leaves
The dark green allele becomes less common
Every beetle in the population turns dark green
b.why: Dark green beetles are eaten less, so more of them survive and breed. Their allele becomes more common in the population. Individual beetles do not change colour to suit the leaves, because selection acts on alleles that are already present.
b.clue: Which beetles are more likely to have offspring?

a.best: Individuals with suited traits leave more offspring

b.best: The dark green allele becomes more common

problems.detail: The distractor 'Individuals with suited traits live longer lives only' puts 'only' awkwardly at the end, so the sentence is clumsy and unclear. It also uses an absolute word in an option. Rewording it, for example as 'Individuals with suited traits live longer but have no more offspring', would make the intended contrast clear.
